quest.title: Silent Seeker of Knowledge
quest.description: According to Tighnari, the Akademiya researcher Haypasia, who lives alone in the forest, is the ideal person to direct Irminsul-related queries to.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x625, Primogem x30, Mora x25450, Recipe: Pita Pocket x1, Hero's Wit x2, Mystic Enhancement Ore x4

chapter.title: Through Mists of Smoke and Forests Dark

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hellooo? Haypasia? Hey, there's nobody here...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, maybe she went out to look for some food. Let's try looking around the area!

dialogues.speaker: Faint Sound
dialogues.text: Clatter...

choices.text: (What was that sound?)

response.speaker: Player
response.text: (It's Haypasia! Is she okay?)

choices.text: (It sounds like it's coming from inside the cave...)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There you are.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Haypasia! Are you alright?

dialogues.speaker: Haypasia
dialogues.text: Uh, ughhh... So hungry... *cough* Need... water...

choices.text: She looks famished!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: There's no way we can get her to eat in her current condition. Let's try finding some water first.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Wait! Why does it look super foggy outside all of a sudden? Anyway, let's go look around!

choices.text: She somehow has more energy than I expected.

talks.objective: Check on how Haypasia is doing

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? How'd things out here end up looking like this?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wh—What happened!? And where are we?

choices.text: Relax, Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Really? Oh, maybe you're right... Let's go investigate the area.

choices.text: There must be a logical explanation for all this.

talks.objective: Proceed onward and go through the tree hollow

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So you came across an Aranara here, and they caused you to have a dream.

dialogues.speaker: Haypasia
dialogues.text: Ah, so that's what they're called... An Aranara. So... not only can you see those creatures, but you're quite familiar with them, too.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Yes, we've bumped into them before.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Just out of curiosity, Haypasia, how is it that you see the Aranara, but don't know anything about them? You didn't even know what they were called.

dialogues.speaker: Haypasia
dialogues.text: Ah, well you see, they've never actually spoken with me directly, and I've never asked anyone about them... Though, I did begin to sense that these Aranara, as you call them, have some sort of deeper connection with the Dendro Archon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Really? How could you sense that?

talks.objective: Try to get to the special cave

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, Paimon gets it, you must have startled them.

dialogues.speaker: Haypasia
dialogues.text: Hehe, yes, apparently I did. I admit that I still feel guilty about that...

dialogues.speaker: Haypasia
dialogues.text: Given that you're familiar with the Aranara, you probably already know that they don't have ill intentions when forcing you into dreams. They only do so to give themselves a chance to run away.

choices.text: Yes, that's what thought, too.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You know, Haypasia, the fact that the nearby Aranara not only often appear around you but also came to your rescue shows that they've taken a real liking to you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon bets it won't be long before your neighbor starts talking to you and becomes your close friend.

response.speaker: Haypasia
response.text: Thank you, I hope that day comes soon. Ah, before I forget, Tighnari mentioned in his letter that you have questions for me regarding Irminsul...?

choices.text: It's because the Aranara are very timid creatures.

dialogues.speaker: Haypasia
dialogues.text: I feel like they aren't as afraid of me as the first time I approached them, but I never would have expected them to save me.

choices.text: What fascinating creatures.

response.speaker: Haypasia
response.text: Yes, no doubt about that. By the way, Tighnari mentioned in his letter that you had questions for me regarding Irminsul...

choices.text: Sounds like a great neighbor.

talks.objective: Keep looking for a path to the upper level of the tree hollow

dialogues.speaker: A Curious Sound
dialogues.text: *rumbling*

dialogues.speaker: Haypasia
dialogues.text: Ehehe... Sorry about that. Sounds like just drinking juice still isn't quite enough for my stomach.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, if somebody hadn't dropped the food earlier...! Ugh, anyway, looks like we'll need to prepare something ourselves. Besides, Paimon's getting hungry too! Let's eat first and talk about Irminsul later.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright, we're up, Traveler! Today's menu will feature Sweet Madame and a Radish Veggie Soup! You'll love them, Haypasia. They're our specialties, after all!

dialogues.speaker: Haypasia
dialogues.text: *drooling* Sounds good! Oh, I've never tried any dishes from other nations before. I certainly look forward to it! It's been so long since I've had a decent meal, too. To be honest, the last time had to be when Tighnari came to visit.

talks.objective: Investigate the courtyard far down the corridor
Investigate the corridor on the other side

dialogues.speaker: Abyss Herald
dialogues.text: Hahaha! Well, well, well. Looks like we meet again, Traveler!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah! The Abyss Herald! What are you plotting to do in this strange place?

dialogues.speaker: Abyss Herald
dialogues.text: Strange place? Plotting? Hehehe... You needn't worry about such things, they don't concern you!

dialogues.speaker: Haypasia
dialogues.text: I know this because the first time I saw them was also the exact day my consciousness was able to form a connection with Irminsul.

dialogues.speaker: Haypasia
dialogues.text: Even after I opened my eyes and stopped meditating, my heart was still pounding and my mind was racing with all the knowledge that I had touched.

dialogues.speaker: Haypasia
dialogues.text: And at that very moment, I suddenly noticed a small figure at the opening of the cave.

dialogues.speaker: Haypasia
dialogues.text: In my curiosity, I began to walk over to the creature. They must have already been used to me living in the cave, because they didn't seem to mind me approaching them. They just kept doing whatever they were up to.

dialogues.speaker: Haypasia
dialogues.text: It wasn't until I crouched down next to them that they suddenly realized that I could see them.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, and then?

dialogues.speaker: Haypasia
dialogues.text: And then, I had a dream... By the time I came to, they were nowhere to be seen.

dialogues.speaker: Haypasia
dialogues.text: I was convinced they'd never show up again, but sure enough, I saw them nearby a few days later... and they weren't alone.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Wh—Why can't we beat this guy...? Paimon doesn't get it. We've faced others like him before — what's wrong this time?

dialogues.speaker: Abyss Herald
dialogues.text: Traveler, though you may have managed to avert countless crises before, your good fortune was bound to end sooner or later. It's time you realize how weak and powerless you really are!

choices.text: My journey will not end here!

response.speaker: Abyss Herald
response.text: #Your {M#sister}{F#brother}? Mwahahaha! Oh, pitiful Traveler, are you really so ignorant? Or are you just living in complete denial?

response.speaker: Abyss Herald
response.text: #{M#Her Highness}{F#His Highness} has long since forsaken you. Your meager existence in {M#her}{F#his} eyes is that of an annoying bug only to be stepped upon!

response.speaker: Abyss Herald
response.text: The bonds of love and family which drive you to find your sibling are utterly gone! Your journey is meaningless!

response.speaker: Abyss Herald
response.text: But don't you fret now. Today will be your last. Now die!

choices.text: #I still must find my {M#sister}{F#brother}!

talks.objective: Make some food by the fireside

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You cook up some dishes over the fire.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: All done! Let's use the empty box that Tighnari gave us since we already washed it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ohhh, it smells amazing! And the box is a nice touch, too. Let's go serve this up and start eating with Haypasia!

talks.objective: Give Haypasia the food you made for her

dialogues.speaker: Ghulam
dialogues.text: Think about it, Tighnari, refusing to join is tantamount to burying your head in the sand!

dialogues.speaker: Ghulam
dialogues.text: I understand that you're a Forest Watcher and that it's your duty to combat the effects of Withering Zones, but isn't it evident that such work is not a lasting solution to the problem?

dialogues.speaker: Ghulam
dialogues.text: As Sage Khajeh clearly stated, your presence and guidance in Sumeru City is pivotal in finding a cure for Irminsul. How could you possibly refuse!?

dialogues.speaker: Khajeh
dialogues.text: Keep your emotions in check, Ghulam. Let's at least listen to Tighnari's reason for declining. We're here to invite him to the Akademiya, not to cause a scene.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Sage Khajeh, I am truly honored that you came here in person, but I'm afraid I must still decline your invitation.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I am merely a Forest Watcher. How could the great minds of the Haravatat have any need of someone like me?

dialogues.speaker: Khajeh
dialogues.text: Haha, well it turns out that your refusal letter had some implications on your master's reputation. He is a renowned Sage of the Amurta, after all. So now, I've come here in his stead.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I see. Huh... Well, I figured that, given his temper, he would come here and berate me personally.

dialogues.speaker: Khajeh
dialogues.text: Tighnari, your master is an integral part of this effort, and now he requires your assistance.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: And what exactly does my master need of me, Sage Khajeh?

dialogues.speaker: Khajeh
dialogues.text: You'll know, once you've arrived in Sumeru City, that is.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: And how long will I be required to stay?

dialogues.speaker: Khajeh
dialogues.text: There's no definite answer as of now.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Do you mean to tell me that despite coming all the way here to Gandharva Ville, you still can't answer the questions I laid out in the letter to my master?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: If that's the case, then I'm afraid I cannot give you a definite answer either.

dialogues.speaker: Ghulam
dialogues.text: Tighnari! But you—

dialogues.speaker: Khajeh
dialogues.text: *sigh* So be it... Come, Ghulam, we're leaving.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh Tighnari, what was that all about?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: It's nothing. Some people from the Akademiya wanted me to go to Sumeru City to assist them with a project, but I had to refuse on account of all my responsibilities here.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: But all that can wait, how did things go with Haypasia?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It was quite the eventful trip! But the main thing is that she's safe and sound. She answered a bunch of questions for us, too.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: #Very good. Now that {NICKNAME} has made a full recovery, there shouldn't be any reason for you to tarry here longer. I assume you will be heading to Sumeru City, correct?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's right! We want to meet Lesser Lord Kusanali and ask her for advice. Do you have any idea on how we can find her?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Sorry, I'm afraid I don't have any advice for you there.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, do you at least know anyone we can try asking in Sumeru City?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Hmm, let me think... My trips to Sumeru City have been fairly short, and most of my acquaintances are researchers...

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Oh, how about this... I'll write you a letter of introduction that you can give to a researcher I know. He's from the Amurta Darshan and is adept at gathering information. Asking him might prove worthwhile.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Also, when you enter Sumeru City, you'll probably end up receiving something like this item here. I'm not sure if it will ever come in handy for you, but maybe you can give it a try.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh? What is it?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: It's called an Akasha Terminal. It's a tool produced by the Akademiya that utilizes the legacy of Greater Lord Rukkhadevata. Some say that this item is the very basis of Sumeru's reputation as the City of Wisdom.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Needless to say, this device and its usage fall under the Akademiya's expertise, so I'll leave it to them to show you how to use it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Great! Next stop, Sumeru City! Ah, but wait, before that...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We need to say goodbye to Collei.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's right! Tighnari, we have something important to say to Collei before we leave. Is she doing better now?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Yes, she's doing much better. After being confined to her bed all this time, I thought a little walk would do her some good. Last I saw her, she was taking the path towards the north crossing.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: She knew you two would be leaving soon, so she must have wanted to see you off.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Thanks, Tighnari! Alright, let's go.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Farewell, and good luck to you both.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: After a delicious meal together, you tell Haypasia about connecting with Irminsul...

dialogues.speaker: Haypasia
dialogues.text: Even though everything you mentioned was in Tighnari's letter, it's still hard to believe you were able to connect with Irminsul... immediately after smelling Spirit Borneol for the first time.

dialogues.speaker: Haypasia
dialogues.text: It took me nearly three years before I could do so... And everyone at the Akademiya even lauded me as a genius.

dialogues.speaker: Haypasia
dialogues.text: You should know that some researchers spend their entire lives without ever successfully connecting with Irminsul as you have.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So why does this incense allow people to connect to Irminsul?

dialogues.speaker: Haypasia
dialogues.text: The ingredients used to make Spirit Borneol primarily consist of plants created by Greater Lord Rukkhadevata. These special ingredients are conducive to heightening our senses to the Dendro Archon's power.

dialogues.speaker: Haypasia
dialogues.text: Since the root of the Dendro Archon's power lies within Irminsul, we can occasionally tap into her powers to peer into the depths of the earth.

choices.text: I think I understand.

response.speaker: Haypasia
response.text: Naturally. Anyone who can establish a connection with Irminsul on their first ever attempt must be a person of great understanding.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Hmm, makes sense... But Paimon's got a question! Why was {M#he}{F#she} sensitive to the smell of those plants for such a long time?

response.speaker: Haypasia
response.text: #That was primarily due to {M#his}{F#her} body's unique constitution. Stimulated by the incense, {M#he}{F#she} could perceive the Dendro Archon's power and experienced a sensory overload, hence the adverse reactions.

response.speaker: Haypasia
response.text: Taking in any scent similar to the ingredients of Spirit Borneol would cause adverse effects.

response.speaker: Haypasia
response.text: Not to worry, though. It appears you have already fully recovered.

response.speaker: Haypasia
response.text: Technically, your body should still be sensitive to the powers of the Dendro Archon, but unless you are using intentional meditation techniques, the scent of Spirit Borneol should no longer trigger such reactions.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whew, well that's a relief.

response.speaker: Haypasia
response.text: I must admit, I am quite envious of your abilities. Even if it meant suffering from pounding headaches for the rest of my life, I'd consider it worthwhile so long as I could connect with Irminsul at will.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa, you're really serious about this whole thing, aren't you?

response.speaker: Haypasia
response.text: Haha, I am a researcher, after all.

response.speaker: Haypasia
response.text: As a member of the Rtawahist Darshan at the Akademiya, my main area of research is the stars and their connection to the fate of living beings. But there is still so much we don't know, especially regarding the mysteries that lie in the starry skies.

response.speaker: Haypasia
response.text: Which is why I must turn to the all-knowing Irminsul for answers.

response.speaker: Haypasia
response.text: If only my perception wasn't so limited... Unfortunately, I cannot guarantee that my every attempt to attune with Irminsul will be successful, or that doing so will leave my consciousness intact.

response.speaker: Haypasia
response.text: I am currently in the stage of training known as "Satyavada Life." Many researchers in Sumeru have lost their minds while seeking to attune with Irminsul during this stage.

response.speaker: Haypasia
response.text: Sages have said that Irminsul contains divine knowledge, and touching such knowledge without the proper preparations and abilities will only lead to one's mind caving in on itself.

response.speaker: Haypasia
response.text: That's why we meditate alone. We need to ensure that our minds will be calm while minimizing the possibility of involving anyone else.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa, so knowledge from Irminsul can be super dangerous! Don't you ever feel afraid of the risk, Haypasia?

response.speaker: Haypasia
response.text: Of course I do, especially during nights that are pitch black with no moonlight, and dead silent without even the sound of insects.

response.speaker: Haypasia
response.text: However, I've been feeling better as of late. I don't get as scared anymore knowing that I have a little neighbor living nearby.

response.speaker: Haypasia
response.text: I believe that being able to see them is a sort of blessing from the Dendro Archon.

response.speaker: Haypasia
response.text: Heh, but what's strangest of all is that they're clearly an envoy of the God of Wisdom herself, and they have the curious power to make people dream.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What's so strange about that? It doesn't sound so out of place for a divine being, does it?

response.speaker: Haypasia
response.text: Well, it's strange because nearly nobody in Sumeru can ever dream.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Is that true?

response.speaker: Haypasia
response.text: Yes... Well, to an extent. Only children can dream in Sumeru. Adults, however, never do.

response.speaker: Haypasia
response.text: The sages say that wisdom implies rationality, but that which occurs in dreams is often neither rational nor logical.

choices.text: Reminds me of the dream I saw from the Aranara...

response.speaker: Haypasia
response.text: Yes, if one struggles with anxieties, those emotions could influence their dreams.

response.speaker: Haypasia
response.text: The fact that the people of Sumeru do not have dreams is seen as a blessing by the sages. They believe that Greater Lord Rukkhadevata, the God of Wisdom, is keeping us away from the foolish delusions you encounter in your sleep.

response.speaker: Haypasia
response.text: I was born into a family of scholars in Sumeru City. Ever since I was a child, my parents would always tell me that I'll know I've grown up once I stop dreaming.

response.speaker: Haypasia
response.text: I studied hard, enrolled as a student in the Akademiya, and went on to become a researcher. *sigh* Sure enough, I never dreamed again.

response.speaker: Haypasia
response.text: But then, on the day I scared the little Aranara... I suddenly saw a dream again.

response.speaker: Haypasia
response.text: It was incredible. Though I don't exactly remember what I saw, I clearly recall the feeling... I suddenly felt like I was a child again.

response.speaker: Haypasia
response.text: Back then, I was foolish and ignorant as any youth would be, but I was free of fear... Maybe dreaming isn't as bad as we've made it out to be.

response.speaker: Haypasia
response.text: Ahem... Just be sure not to speak of this if you travel to Sumeru City. They'll look at you as if you've lost your mind.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #So do you have any thoughts about the things {M#he}{F#she} saw when {M#he}{F#she} connected with Irminsul?

response.speaker: Haypasia
response.text: Sorry, I'm afraid I don't have any answers as of now. All I can say is that what you saw is a memory contained within Irminsul itself.

response.speaker: Haypasia
response.text: Hmm... "world... forget me..." What could that possibly mean?

response.speaker: Haypasia
response.text: Agh, if only I could ascend past Satyavada Life and begin Paripurna Life, I might have some more answers for you.

response.speaker: Haypasia
response.text: *sigh* If you two are ever in the area again, please be sure to come and see me.

choices.text: Thanks, Haypasia!

response.speaker: Haypasia
response.text: There's no need to be thanking me, you two are my saviors! Besides, I'm already looking forward to tasting some more of your cooking, hehe.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You continue chatting before settling down for a good night's rest.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Now that we know Haypasia is alright and had the chance to ask her some questions, Paimon thinks it's about time to head back to Gandharva Ville.

choices.text: We wish you luck in your endeavors.
It was a big, chaotic mess...
Sorry, you lost me there...

response.speaker: Haypasia
response.text: That's alright, I'm sure you'll come to a clearer understanding as you remain in Sumeru.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Ah, I've been waiting for you two.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: I, uh... Well... ugh, never mind. I guess I should just wish you two a safe and successful journey.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Thanks for waiting here just to see us off, Collei. We're headed to Sumeru City.

choices.text: Please take care of yourself, Collei.

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: Don't worry about me, I can take care of myself. My condition won't be getting in the way of my duties. I want to be a Forest Ranger, after all! It's up to me and the others to protect the rainforest here.

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: And uh, well I'm sorry... I should have told you both about my condition when we first met. I just wanted you two to treat me as a normal friend, not some girl that needs your sympathy...

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: But I guess now I understand that the most important thing is for friends to be genuine with one another.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: There's no need to apologize, Collei! We should be thanking you for trusting us enough to be your friends and sharing your past with us.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We're probably still gonna worry about your condition, but that's because we're friends and we care about you!

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: Thank you, that means a lot... Uh, before you leave, I have something for you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh? What is it?

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: It's my recipe for Pita Pockets! I told you that I'd give you a copy, remember? My handwriting is a little messy, so please don't laugh.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yay, thanks Collei! Now we can eat those scrumptious little pitas whenever and wherever we like!

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: I hope that whenever you eat them, you'll both remember your time here in Gandharva Ville.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Of course, we will!

response.speaker: Collei
response.text: Well then, I, Trainee Forest Ranger Collei, bid you both farewell. Please visit Gandharva Ville again. The rangers will always be ready to assist you here.

choices.text: We'll be back to see you soon, Collei.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Ugh! Huh...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (What was all that just now? Strange... It feels like I was just dreaming for a moment there, but I can't remember what I saw...)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm, what do we do? We haven't seen Haypasia anywhere out here...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, there she is! Quick, let's see how she's doing.

dialogues.speaker: Haypasia
dialogues.text: So sweet... Mmm...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, the good news is that she's still conscious. Hey! Why'd you drop her food on the floor like that!?

choices.text: Sorry, I uh... kinda zoned out for a second there.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, are you okay? That's really not like you...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Anyways, we can talk about this later. We'd better make sure she's alright first.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Whoa, wait a sec! Look at all this fruit lying around her. We can put that to good use!

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: After giving the semi-conscious Haypasia some water and fruit juice...

response.speaker: Haypasia
response.text: Ugh... Who's there!? Tighnari, is that you? Ah!

response.speaker: Haypasia
response.text: Huh?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's okay, you can relax, Haypasia. Tighnari sent us here to bring you some food and water. Here, we have a letter that he asked us to give you.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You give Haypasia the letter from Tighnari.

response.speaker: Haypasia
response.text: I see, so you're friends of Tighnari. I apologize for all the trouble I've caused you.

response.speaker: Haypasia
response.text: I'm grateful that you came so quickly to save me. You even brought all this fruit.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh well, actually, we didn't bring the fruit. It was already here when we arrived.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We were kinda wondering about that, actually. When we found you here, there was all this fruit lying around and even some juice dripping from your lips... Uh, how did you end up like this anyway?

response.speaker: Haypasia
response.text: Oh? Really?

response.speaker: Haypasia
response.text: Hmm, I seem to understand now. All the fruit was likely from my, uh... neighbor. Must have come by and saw me like this.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Your neighbor? You mean there's someone else living nearby?

choices.text: Is it a little round creature?

response.speaker: Haypasia
response.text: Oh? So you're able to see them, too?

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You tell Haypasia and Paimon everything that happened after entering the cave.

choices.text: Kind of like... a cabbage?
Sorry, seeing Haypasia must have given me a shock.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, guess that makes sense... She does look kinda rough at the moment.

dialogues.speaker: Haypasia
dialogues.text: Are you already finished cooking? Mmmm, smells delectable! I'm truly thankful whenever I can enjoy a proper meal like this. Cooking really isn't my forte...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait, hold on a second, Traveler! You say that before we arrived, you saw some mysterious creature and suddenly had a strange dream? Isn't that a little too crazy to believe?

dialogues.speaker: Haypasia
dialogues.text: No, I actually do believe what the Traveler is saying. I myself had a similar experience once before and ended up scaring my timid, little neighbor here.

dialogues.speaker: Haypasia
dialogues.text: You needn't worry — he means you no harm. He only dragged you into the dream because he hoped to buy himself a little time in order to scurry away.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So Haypasia, just what kind of creature is your neighbor exactly?

dialogues.speaker: Haypasia
dialogues.text: I'm not sure what it's called, to be honest... But I do know that they have some sort of deeper connection with the Dendro Archon.

dialogues.speaker: Haypasia
dialogues.text: So... hungry...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, this place is huge!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon knew there's something off about that cave! Let's think of a way to get over there and have a closer look. Who knows, maybe we'll find a lead of some kind!
